title: Republic Act No. 170 — An Act Creating the City of Dagupan (Supreme Court E-Library)
licence: © Supreme Court E-Library 2019 (site footer)
notes: The Supreme Court E-Library's text of the charter, headed "H. No. 1204 / 43 OG No. 7, 2690 (July, 1947)" and "[ REPUBLIC ACT NO. 170, June 20, 1947 ]". Section 1: "This Act shall be known as the Charter of the City of Dagupan." Section 2: the city, "which is hereby created, shall comprise the present territorial jurisdiction of the municipality of Dagupan, in the Province of Pangasinan", and the President may by executive order add contiguous barrios or municipalities. Section 7: the Mayor "shall be appointed by the President of the Philippines". Section 11: a Municipal Board of the Mayor and eight councilors elected at large. Section 88: the city government "shall be organized on such a date as may be fixed by the President". Section 89: the city "shall continue as part of the second representative district of the Province of Pangasinan". Section 90: "This Act shall take effect upon its approval. Approved, June 20, 1947." `data_as_of` is the approval date the text states; the E-Library gives no date for its own edition, so `published` is null. The Official Gazette's website returned HTTP 403 to the request, so the Gazette edition this text cites was not read directly. The E-Library prints titles in capitals; they are given here in title case.

title: Executive Order No. 96 — Fixing the Date of Organization and Territorial Jurisdiction of the City of Dagupan (Supreme Court E-Library)
licence: © Supreme Court E-Library 2019 (site footer)
notes: Headed "43 OG No. 11, 4554 (November 1947)" and "[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 96, October 15, 1947 ]", and signed "this 15th day of October" 1947 by President Manuel Roxas. It fixes "the first of January, nineteen hundred and forty-eight, as the date for the organization of the City of Dagupan and qualification of the City Mayor and Members of the Municipal Board appointed in accordance with section 88 of Republic Act No. 170", and provides that upon that organization "the municipality of Calasiao shall be joined to, and made an integral part of, said City". Executive Order No. 115 (sc-elibrary-eo-115-1947) later refers to this order as "dated October 1, 1947"; the order's own heading and signature both say 15 October, which is the date published.

licence: © Supreme Court E-Library 2019 (site footer)
notes: Headed "44 OG No. 1, 12 (January 1948)" and "[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 115, December 31, 1947 ]", and signed "this 31st day of December" 1947 by President Manuel Roxas. It again fixes "the first of January, nineteen hundred and forty-eight, as the date for the organization of the City of Dagupan and qualification of the City Mayor and Members of the Municipal Board appointed in accordance with section 88 of said Act", provides that "Unless the President shall hereafter order otherwise the City of Dagupan shall ... comprise the present territorial jurisdiction of the municipality of Dagupan", and modifies the inconsistent provisions of Executive Order No. 96. It fixes a date; it does not itself record that the organization took place on it.

title: Republic Act No. 484 — An Act to Amend the Chapter of the City of Dagupan (Supreme Court E-Library)
licence: © Supreme Court E-Library 2019 (site footer)
notes: Headed "H. No. 1137 / 46 OG No. 7, 2990 (July, 1950)" and "[ REPUBLIC ACT NO. 484, June 10, 1950 ]"; "Chapter" in the title is as printed. It amends Section 11 of the charter so that the Municipal Board is "composed of the Mayor, who shall be its presiding officer, the City Treasurer, the City Engineer, the City Attorney, the City Health Officer, and four councilors who shall be elected at large by popular vote", and inserts Section 89-A: "The voters of the City of Dagupan shall be qualified to vote for the offices of provincial governor and members of the provincial board of the Province of Pangasinan." It also amends Sections 7 (the Mayor's salary), 12 and 85. "This Act shall take effect upon its approval ... Approved, June 10, 1950." Republic Act No. 2259 (sc-elibrary-ra-2259-1959) later names Dagupan among the cities whose voters "shall not vote for provincial officials".

title: Republic Act No. 2259 — An Act Making Elective the Offices of Mayor, Vice-Mayor and Councilors in Chartered Cities (Supreme Court E-Library)
licence: © Supreme Court E-Library 2019 (site footer)
notes: Headed "S. No. 2 / 55 OG No. 30, 5705 (July 27, 1959)" and "[ REPUBLIC ACT NO. 2259, June 19, 1959 ]". The full title continues "... Regulating the Election in Such Cities and Fixing the Salaries and Tenure of Such Offices". A general law, not a Dagupan statute, but it names the city. Section 1: "The offices of Mayor, Vice-Mayor, and members of the city council or municipal board in all chartered cities in the Philippines which are now filled by appointment are hereby declared elective." Section 2: "the qualified voters of cities shall vote or shall not vote for officials as their respective charters provide, in the cities of Iloilo and Dagupan where the said voters shall not vote for provincial officials." Section 3 creates the position of Vice-Mayor where a charter has none. Section 8 excludes Manila, Cavite, Trece Martires and Tagaytay only. "Approved, June 19, 1959." No consequence for the city's present classification is drawn from it here.
